title: Hired by Johnny Carey and Mal Frazier for the Nest
summary: Wooding recalls how a war buddy sent him to Carey and Frazier, who hired him on a gentleman's agreement with no contract.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when we come back off the road from

the "Plantation Days" where we got stranded and we had helped and all all the girls get home. I run into an old buddy of mine from the war. And he said, "Sam, what are you doing." And I said, "Doing nothing and going nowhere fast." So, he said to me, "Well, how would you like to go down to Johnny Carey and MAL Frazier, they are opening a new club. And they're looking for an orchestra leader and they'll put a band in there, and I said, "What size band?" And he said, "Well, you come on and see Johnny." And Johnny did more of the business than Mal. They were two sportsmen that had been around there in Harlem. In fact, they were king of that, and they had been under Baron Wilkins' tutelage and they were pretty good. Anyhow, so I went down to see them and they were just putting up a rag decoration in the place. And Johnny said to me, "Well I heard that you didn't have much luck out on the road, and I know you from Old Man Baron's place, how would you like to work for us?" Well, we got together and the money was satisfactory, so I said, "Sure, I'll be happy to come in here." And he said, "Well, we're going to open in about six weeks." "By the time this place is finished and we get a little revue together." And he said, "now, you start getting the band together." And we didn't have no contract. Because in those days, we didn't bother about a contract when you'd know people was straight and all like that and we'd worked together. I worked together with the man that sent me to Europe and never had a contract. You see, in those days,
it was a gentleman's agreement. If you can call them gentlemen.
